concedes: Lens 5 (tournament documents and formats), round 3. The user's latest revision counts every other player as a loser of a one-winner free-for-all game and carves out draws, team games and any game type whose starting player the CR already settles (103.1b, 904.12c). I re-checked the tournament documents and formats against that wording. MTR 2.2 gives the choice to 'the loser of that game' in a two-player match and has no multiplayer wording, so it does not address several losers. MTR 9.3 (Two-Headed Giant) is a team game and is carved out. A search of the MTR finds 'multiplayer' only in 7.2 (Conspiracy boosters), which is irrelevant, and the JAR has no section mentioning Commander. reference/formats/matches.md says no official rule says who starts a later game of a multiplayer match, and its only answer (random first player) is level 4, which cannot override a level 1 or 2 text and does not contradict a gap-filling stipulation. commander.md defers to matches.md and sets no different start rule. MTR 2.5 allows concession and intentional draws, but draws are outside the rule and nothing in the rule rewards a concession. No tournament rule or REL settles the gap or changes the stipulation, and the rule contradicts no MTR, IPG or format text. Residual weaknesses that are not refutations: 'cannot agree' in the tie-break is undefined, and the Game Loss penalty in a multiplayer game is not spelled out.

concede_evidence.heading: Conceding or Intentionally Drawing Games or Matches
concede_evidence.excerpt:
Until the result of a match has been recorded, players may concede or mutually agree to a draw in that game or
match. If the conceding player won a game in the match, the match must be reported as 2-1. Intentional draws
where no games were played are always reported as 0-0-3 in EventLink.
